article_title: Increasing Parental Involvement to Promote Dropout Prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian Lower Secondary Schools
citation: Gianluca Argentin, Gian Paolo Barbetta, Francesca Maci. (2016). Increasing parental involvement to promote dropout prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian lower secondary schools. SREE Spring 2016 Conference. https://www.sree.org/
title: Family Group Conference (FGC) in schools
description: FGC is "a world widespread participatory approach" used to help families find their own solutions to problems affecting their lives. In schools it is a structured meeting between family members, professionals and significant others that produces a common plan for a pupil's school life; the referrer is the school rather than child-protection services. It is a family-led decision-making process based on the empowerment of families and children, combining family knowledge with professional knowledge.
requirements: A co-ordinator who is independent, trusts the strengths of the family, understands the child's needs, believes in the model, and is flexible, friendly and able to work autonomously
constraints: In the school variant the referrer is the school and concerns focus on the pupil's school life rather than family relationships and care
target_learners: at-risk 6th and 7th graders in lower secondary school
examples: 84 of the 131 students assigned to treatment accepted and received an FGC between November 2013 and April 2014 in the Garbagnatese district of Lombardy.
key_sources: Gianluca Argentin, Gian Paolo Barbetta, Francesca Maci. (2016). Increasing parental involvement to promote dropout prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian lower secondary schools. SREE Spring 2016 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED567232

article_title: Increasing Parental Involvement to Promote Dropout Prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian Lower Secondary Schools
citation: Gianluca Argentin, Gian Paolo Barbetta, Francesca Maci. (2016). Increasing parental involvement to promote dropout prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian lower secondary schools. SREE Spring 2016 Conference. https://www.sree.org/
title: FGC as a family-led empowerment model
description: The article describes FGC not simply as a social work intervention but as "a cultural approach based on the strong principle of 'empowerment' of families and children". The model assumes families are experts about their own problems and can take control and make safe decisions for young people with support from welfare services. The FGC builds an alliance between families and professionals to share power and responsibilities in decision making involving a child, with a co-ordinator acting as a relational guide for the family.
requirements: Collaboration between the family and social services to make a plan for the well-being of a child in need
target_learners: children and young people with school or welfare concerns
target_learning_goals: enable families to devise the best possible plan for their children
key_sources: Gianluca Argentin, Gian Paolo Barbetta, Francesca Maci. (2016). Increasing parental involvement to promote dropout prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian lower secondary schools. SREE Spring 2016 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED567232

title: Garbagnatese FGC randomized controlled trial
description: An individual-level RCT, blocking on schools, in a social district of 7 cities in the province of Milan. Of 262 referred at-risk students, 131 were assigned to treatment (84 treated) and 131 to control. Randomization created equivalence on a large subset of observed variables; attrition rates were "negligible and balanced". Outcomes came from pre- and post-intervention questionnaires, school administrative data, and national standardized tests, with ITT and IV-based ATT estimates.
requirements: Pre-intervention measures used as covariates to gain statistical power, and blocking on schools
constraints: Sample size was smaller than assumed in the original design due to only 262 referred students
key_sources: Gianluca Argentin, Gian Paolo Barbetta, Francesca Maci. (2016). Increasing parental involvement to promote dropout prevention. Lessons from an RCT in Italian lower secondary schools. SREE Spring 2016 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED567232

article_title: An analysis of educational needs to enhance the response competency of infectious disease control personnel to emerging infectious diseases.
citation: Jeong Sun Young, Choi Sungae, Kim Jaeyeun, Lee Sojin, Park Young-soon, Chun Kyunghee. (2026). An analysis of educational needs to enhance the response competency of infectious disease control personnel to emerging infectious diseases. Korean Journal of Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.3946/kjme.2025.115
title: Semi-structured focus group interview guide for infectious disease training needs assessment
description: A semi-structured interview guide developed in three steps: literature and guideline review, expert validation by a panel of three specialists, and pilot testing. The finalized guide covered three domains: "training experiences and challenges in practice, required field competencies, and educational needs by occupational group." Questions were tailored to each participant's role with flexibility for emerging themes.
requirements: expert panel validation for clarity and relevance
pilot interview to test flow and clarity
constraints: Questions tailored to each participant's role, so domains were adapted per occupational group
target_learners: healthcare and non-healthcare infectious disease control personnel
target_learning_goals: identifying training needs and field competencies
examples: Used with 34 participants recruited via snowball sampling across 16 healthcare workers, 15 administrative staff, and three government officials
